rationale: B wins by a nose because it finds the cleaner, harder reporter wedge: "Warby Parker says store shoppers spend more than online buyers. It will not say how much." A's best line, "the historically defensible, insurance-tied part of the optical business the incumbents have owned," is smart, but A spends two angles circling the exam-room story from different altitudes. B still needs a leash on "it is the reason the whole expansion exists," but the standalone data angle gives the founder more usable strategic material.
gaps_in_A: "A DTC eyewear brand is quietly becoming a place you get your eyes checked" overlaps with the optometrist/incumbent angle; it needs real outside retail-health evidence or it is just the same exam story in a different coat.

"the historically defensible, insurance-tied part of the optical business the incumbents have owned" imports industry context not supplied in the update; use it as a reporting hypothesis, not a fact in the pitch.
"Warby Parker bets its next 40 stores on the optometrist" slightly outruns the supplied "most new stores" fact; the exact staffed-store count is load-bearing.

The pharmacy angle admits it is thin, but "Warby Parker is testing whether you'll buy glasses at the pharmacy counter" still needs the unnamed chain, scope, and locations before it survives a reporter call.
gaps_in_B: "it is the reason the whole expansion exists" is causal overclaim. The update says Warby claims retail customers spend more; it does not prove that claim is the whole rationale for the expansion.
"it is opening 40 stores on the strength of that claim" repeats the same invented causal link in the facts section. Facts sections do not get to launder assumptions.

"Warby Parker built its brand on skipping the middleman" and "made direct-to-consumer eyewear a category" rely on company lore outside the supplied update; not fatal, but it needs care before pitching.
"The category question stays open for as long as the rollout is under way" blunts the why-now. Reporters need June 2026 urgency, not an open-ended rollout meditation.
